sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI  ON THE 6th OF APRIL, 2026  MISC. APPEAL No. 1804 of 2021  RIYAJ KHALIK
Versus  JAGDISH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Shri Himanshu Paliwal - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.3.
 ORDER

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 12/03/2021 passed by Member, III Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in MACC No.46/2015, whereby an amount of Rs.4,03,400/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 18/07/2018 to the appellant / claimant - injured with interest @ 7% per annum.

entities.text: III Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the accident appellant has suffered fractures in Tibia and Fibula bones of left leg and suffered grievous injuries in the legs, waist and hands.

In the accident he has suffered 34.8% disability and Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/194) is available on record, which has been proved by the Dr. Manish Bajaj NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9062 2 MA-1804-2021 (AW-2).

His contention is that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding meager amount of Rs.1,00,000/-, whereas considering the disability at 34.8%
adequate amount should have been awarded in this head.
2.1 Learned counsel further submits that appellant was working as a Private Teacher in Delhi Public School and was a skilled labourer at the time of accident.

His contention is that in case the income is not proved by any cogent evidence, income ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act,
according to which income of the injured on the date of accident comes to Rs.9,360/- per month considering him as 'Skilled Labourer'.
2.2

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has also erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas looking to the age 38 years of the claimant, as per para 59.4 of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40%

sentences.text: 1 amount is to be added in the head of Future Prospects.
According to the age of claimant, multiplier of 15 is to be adopted.
2.3 Learned counsel further submits that consolidated amount of Rs.40,000/- has been awarded in the head of Attendant, Special Diet, Transportation and Pain and Suffering, which is on lower side,
instead thereof adequate amount is to be awarded separately in each and every head.

No amount has been awarded in the head of loss of income for a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9062 3 MA-1804-2021 period of six months, during which was the appellant was unable to perform his work.
Appellant has suffered permanent disability and in future also he has to bear treatment expenses, therefore, in the head of Future Medical Expenses, appropriate amount should have been awarded.
On the aforesaid submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as prayed for.
3 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

5. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
From perusal of the record, it reveals that appellant has suffered fractures in Tibial and Fibula bones and also suffered grievous injuries in various parts of body.
Doctor has given disability to the extent of 34.8.

For this, Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/194) is on record which has been proved by Dr.
Manish Bajaj (AW-2), therefore, looking to the nature and number of injuries at least 15%
permanent disability to the proportion of whole body should have been given.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9062 4 MA-1804-2021 7.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 30/03/2018 appellant was working as Teacher in a private School, however, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, therefore, in the light of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093, income of the injured is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the injured is taken as Rs.9,360/- per month considering him 'Skilled person'.
8. Injured was 38 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra), 40% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Looking to the nature and number of injuries suffered by the appellant the consolidated amount of Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Claims Tribunal in the heads of Attendant, Special Diet,
Riyaj Khalik vs Jagdish on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72601284/
2

Transportation and Paint Suffering appears on lower side, instead thereof, separate amount ought to have been awarded in each and every head, therefore, an amount of Rs.25,000/-, Rs.10,000/-,
Rs.10,000/- and Rs.40,000/- is awarded in the heads of Attendant Expenses, Special Diet,
Transportation and Pain & Sufferings and Loss of Amenities repetitively.

10. Appellant was not able to perform his work during the period NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9062 5 MA-1804-2021 of hospitalization for about 35 days and thereafter,
months together he has suffered loss of income due to the injuries, therefore, in all fairness six months' loss of income is to be added in the amount of compensation.
Considering the gravity of injuries, in the head of Future Medical Expenses, an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- is also added.

11. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
15% PD comes to Rs.3,53,808/-
 Permanent Disability: (Rs.9,360/- + 40% FP x 12 Mont  x Multiplier of 15)
 Medical Expenses: Rs.2,63,372/-
 Future Medical Expenses: Rs.1,50,000/-
 Attendant Expenses: Rs.25,000/-
 Special Diet: Rs.10,000/-
 Transportation: Rs.10,000/-
 Loss of Income: Rs.56,160/- (for Six Months)
 Pain & Suffering and  Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of Amenities:
 Total Amount: Rs.9,08,340/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.4,03,400/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.5,04,940/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.9,08,340/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.4,03,400/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.5,04,940/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Since the appeal has been valued at Rs.3,00,000/- only, therefore, the appellant is directed to pay additional court fees on the rest NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9062 6 MA-1804-2021 of the amount of Rs.2,04,940/- within a period of 30 days from today at the prevailing slab of court fees, thereafter, the same will be disbursed to the appellant.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 7% shall remain intact.
13. Subject to payment of requisite additional court fees within the aforesaid period, the enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellant will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period, till the payment of requisite court fees.
